I added a 0.25s sleep after each sandbox call in `tests/test_payments.py`. I didn't run the test, because it's an integration test that calls the real sandbox.

- **What changed:** a new constant, `SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL_S = 0.25`, with a comment explaining the 5 requests/second limit. `time.sleep(SANDBOX_CALL_INTERVAL_S)` now runs after each `requests.post` in the loop. That keeps the test under 4 requests per second, and the sleep after the last call also spaces this test from whatever runs next.
- **This may not fix the flakes:** the test makes only 4 calls, so on its own it can't go over 5 per second. If CI is still flaky, the extra traffic probably comes from somewhere else, like parallel CI jobs (pytest-xdist workers or concurrent pipelines) using the same sandbox credentials. In that case a retry on HTTP 429 with backoff would be the sturdier fix.

I also saved the 5 requests/second limit to the project's EngramDB memory store, so future sessions and collaborators will know about it when they write sandbox tests.
